keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 25-29; no Cliopatria row, no Wikipedia article of his own. 'Zhang Bu (張步), nominally the Prince of Qi under Liu Yong, but who independently controlled the modern Shandong region.' The Shandong outline is the modern province; no page gives a frontier. Reviewer fix (ea-02-x-fixed): the Shandong outline is cut by the three circles of the liu-yong dossier (Shangqiu 120 km and Xuzhou 100 km, 25-27, whose land goes to the Eastern Han when Suiyang falls in 27; Linyi 70 km, Tanhai, 27-29), so no ground is drawn for two states. One shape for 25-29 rather than a split at 27: after Liu Yong's death the Jiyin-Shanyang country is the Eastern Han's (liu-yong /ledger loss 27), not Zhang Bu's, and the Liu Yong page names no holder of Tanhai before Liu Yu (it only has Dong Xian as Prince of Haixi, a place it does not locate), so the Linyi circle is cut for 25-26 as well; the page is silent there.

ledger.note: 25: Zhang Bu holds Shandong, bridged. The Guangwu page names him among the regional powers Liu Xiu faced after taking the throne in the summer of 25 but dates no rise; the first dated fact is the spring 27 title of Prince of Qi from Liu Yong (Liu Yong page). PAGE SILENT on when he took the land. [Reviewer ea-02-x, 2026-10-19: counterpart changed from lulin (dossier ends 23) to han-dynasty, which carries the Gengshi regime of 23-25]

27: Zhang Bu is made Prince of Qi by Liu Yong. 'In the spring of AD 27, Liu Yong named Zhang Bu as Prince of Qi and Dong Xian as Prince of Haixi' (Liu Yong page; Zhang Bu took the title, the page says nothing more); the Guangwu page says he 'independently controlled the modern Shandong region'. Retyped from rename in the repair pass: the title is a nominal vassalage to Liu Yong (liu-yong /ledger vassal_start 27 names zhang-bu), the land does not change.

ledger.note: 29: Zhang Bu surrenders. 'Zhang, seeing the futility of resistance, surrendered and was created a marquess' (AD 29 passage). Geng Yan page (opened in the repair pass): in the winter (October) of 29 Zhang Bu led about 200,000 men against Geng Yan near Linzi, withdrew at midnight, retreated to Pingshou and surrendered at the army gate; Geng Yan 'raised flags for the twelve commanderies' of his troops; the page gives no month for the surrender and never says marquess, so month stays blank.

notes:
Zhang Bu, Qi 25-29. 2 pages opened (Emperor Guangwu of Han; Liu Yong (Xin dynasty)); no Wikipedia article of his own was found, and Cliopatria has no row. Unsettled: the start year (confidence 1; the Guangwu page gives no date for his rise); the Qi capital (not on any page); the campaign by which the Eastern Han took Shandong. Counterparts: han-dynasty and lulin exist; liu-yong is written by this batch. The 27 'rename' only marks the title; it moves no land.
Repair pass (ea-02-x-fixed): (1) /ledger 27 'rename' is now vassal_start with liu-yong and a vassal_end 27 is added (Liu Yong page reopened: 'In the spring of AD 27, Liu Yong named Zhang Bu as Prince of Qi'; Liu Yong's death in 27, no month). (2) The shape is Shandong minus liu-yong's three circles for 25-29, one keyframe instead of the reviewer's split at 27, because the Jiyin-Shanyang country goes to the Eastern Han (not back to Zhang Bu) when Suiyang falls in 27; Linyi is cut for 25-26 too because the page names no holder of Tanhai before Liu Yu (a hole the pages cannot fill). (3) The Liu Yong page attributes the attack on Jiyin, Shanyang, Pei, Chu, Huaiyang and Runan to Zhou Jian, not directly to Liu Yong; liu-yong's note should be read that way. (4) Identity predecessor changed from lulin to han-dynasty (lulin ends in 23). The Geng Yan page (thin) was not opened; the Qi capital stays unknown. The Geng Yan page (opened for the thin item) gives Zhang Bu's base as Ju County in the 29 campaign (capital entered 25-29 as a bridge), King of Qi by Liu Yong without a year, and the Jinan/Linzi/Pingshou campaign; it is silent on his rise (23-25), on Langya and on any marquess title (that is the Guangwu page). Three pages in all.
